messages:
Maya R.: Quick heads-up — we're switching to a staggered regional rollout for today's v3.9.1 artifacts. Reason: reduced us-west GPU capacity during the maintenance window. A few bullets: 
- Canary in eu-west first, then ap-south, then us-east. us-west will be last and limited to 20% traffic.
- Freeze for non-critical frontend and infra churn for the next 12h. Only hotfixes and rollback-safe patches.
- Fallback policy enabled: if latency > 200ms or error rate > 0.8% for 5m, auto-fail to previous model variant.
Please ack if you're owning watch or have blockers.

Chris S. (SRE): Acked. I'll own the first 90m watch. Setting PagerDuty for release-escalation.

Anjali P.: Can you paste the canary check commands? I'll run the traffic split after deploy.

Maya R.: Sure — use these for the routing policy test:
```
# check canary status
curl -sS https://internal-api.redwood/rollouts/v3.9.1/status | jq .canaries
# simulate 5% traffic to canary
redwood-cli traffic set --service inference --region eu-west --percent 5 --release v3.9.1
```
If any test fails, revert with `redwood-cli rollout revert --release v3.9.1`.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started: v3.9.1 -> eu-west (id: canary-2003). Logs: https://ci.redwood/build/2003

Theo L.: Noted on the failover thresholds. I'm going to increase the KV cache TTL for eu-west by +10s to reduce cold-starts during the canary.

Jas K.: Heads-up for product: The new prompt-sanitizer tweak is in this release — minor changes to token counting. QA already signed off on core paths. Expect slight embed cost change in some edge calls.

Chris S. (SRE): Canary metrics so far (15m): p50=42ms, p95=98ms, errors=0.12%. No regressions. Continuing watch.

Maya R.: Thanks. After eu-west completes we do ap-south canary at 10% then us-east at 40%. us-west stays at 20% until tomorrow morning.

Leo (release lead): Quick policy note — per-runner rule: any rollback after a cross-region deploy requires a short RCA stub in #postmortems with tags: region, cause, mitigation. Keep it one para.

Anjali P.: ap-south canary now set to 10%. Running smoke tests.

deploy-bot: Canary success: eu-west -> pass. Proceeding to ap-south.

Jas K.: Thx team. I'll monitor user-facing logs for prompt sanitization false positives. Ping me if we see >0.5% user-visible rejects.

Chris S. (SRE): ap-south p95=120ms, errors=0.6% — slightly high, pulling traces.

Theo L.: Found a hot retry loop in the webhook fanout in ap-south; patch queued as hotfix-2003. If it spikes, we should throttle webhook fanout to 2 concurrent.

Maya R.: Let's hold the ap-south percentage at 10% while Theo's patch lands. No further increase.

Anjali P.: Patch merged, deploying hotfix-2003 to ap-south canary.

deploy-bot: Hotfix deploy started: hotfix-2003 -> ap-south (id: hf-2003)

Chris S. (SRE): Post-hotfix ap-south: p95=85ms, errors=0.08%. Good to ramp after 10 more minutes of green.

Maya R.: Okay — we'll ramp us-east to 40% after 30m of stable signals across eu-west and ap-south. us-west remains at 20% and in manual-only ramp mode.

Leo (release lead): Also — reminder: release freeze for non-critical PRs is until 2023-11-07T08:00Z (12h from now). If you need an exception, open a freeze-exception with a clear rollback plan.

Jas K.: Noted. I'll coordinate exceptions for any last-minute product tweaks.

Maya R.: Thanks everyone. If anything odd pops, call the release channel and page the oncall. I'll post a short rollout summary in #eng-announcements when we reach full ramp. :rocket:
